source.title: Measurement of Impulsive Thrust from a Closed Radio Frequency Cavity in Vacuum
source.why_relevant: Official NASA Johnson Space Center/Eagleworks report of a tapered RF cavity test campaign in vacuum, including geometry, thrust levels, and a dedicated null-thrust test.
source.quote: A vacuum test campaign evaluating the impulsive thrust performance of a tapered RF test article excited in the TM212 mode at 1,937 megahertz (MHz) has been completed... thrust data from forward, reverse, and null suggests that the system is consistently performing with a thrust to power ratio of 1.2 ± 0.1 mN/kW. The RF resonance test article is a copper frustum with an inner diameter of 27.9 cm on the big end, inner diameter of 15.9 cm on the small end, and an axial length of 22.9 cm... all vacuum tests were performed at or below 8×10−6 Torr. The results from the null thrust testing show no impulsive element in the collected data, only the thermal signal.
source.geometry_or_result: Copper frustum: big-end ID 27.9 cm, small-end ID 15.9 cm, axial length 22.9 cm; 5.4 cm-thick polyethylene disc, 15.6 cm outer diameter; 13.5 mm loop antenna; TM212 at 1,937 MHz. Vacuum ≤ 8×10−6 Torr; power scans 40/60/80 W; reported thrust 1.2 ± 0.1 mN/kW toward narrow end. Null test: three 80 W vacuum runs showed no impulsive element, only thermal signal.

source.title: High-accuracy thrust measurements of the EMDrive and elimination of false-positive effects
source.why_relevant: Peer-reviewed TU Dresden (SpaceDrive project) null test of an EMDrive-like tapered cavity with artifact analysis, published in CEAS Space Journal.
source.quote: Our cavity is based on the same geometry as the one used by White et al.... It consists of a tapered cone, which was mechanically pressed, with a cylindrical flange and a collar made out of 2 mm-thick copper... We found no thrust values within a wide frequency band including several resonance frequencies and different modes. Our data limit any anomalous thrust to below the force equivalent from classical radiation for a given amount of power... rules out previous test results by at least two orders of magnitude.
source.geometry_or_result: Tapered copper cone on White et al.-type geometry, 2 mm-thick copper with cylindrical flange and collar; matched resonance 1,914 MHz, unloaded Q ≈ 23,000 (same paper's TU Dresden conference PDF, opened full text). Result: null — no anomalous thrust above the classical radiation-pressure (photon thrust) level.

source.title: Anomalous Thrust Production from an RF Test Device Measured on a Low-Thrust Torsion Pendulum
source.why_relevant: Official NASA NTRS record of the August 2013 Eagleworks campaign reporting ~30–50 µN from an RF cavity at ambient pressure, including a null test article that nevertheless registered thrust.
source.quote: Approximately 30-50 micro-Newtons of thrust were recorded from an electric propulsion test article consisting primarily of a radio frequency (RF) resonant cavity excited at approximately 935 megahertz... within a stainless steel vacuum chamber with the door closed but at ambient atmospheric pressure. Thrust was observed on both test articles, even though one of the test articles was designed with the expectation that it would not produce thrust... referred to as the 'null' test article.
source.geometry_or_result: RF resonant cavity, ≈935 MHz; ambient atmospheric pressure (chamber door closed, not vacuum); ≈30–50 µN thrust. Null-article confound: thrust appeared on the article designed not to produce thrust.
